look_here_first: POVERTY DROPSEED (*Sporobolus vaginiflorus*): START with genuine Harms SPVA-b1 rooted grass photograph showing thin roots, fine basal blades and attached long flowering culms, then SPVA-i showing BOTH terminal slender flowering head and an additional shorter spikelet-bearing upper-sheath unit. SPVA-J1 shows real bloom structures, SPVA-j2 pointed purple/green one-flowered spikelet components next to source ruler, SPVA-d a real author's disarticulation view, and SPVA-L the short HAIR-FRINGE ligule location (not a large membrane). Presence of an upper-sheath flowering unit DOES NOT alone prove cleistogamy or the precise taxon, since other dropseeds can make closed flowers. Use actual mature lemma micromorphology (hooks/hairs; about 400×) and reliably rooted/source-determined material to resolve S. neglectus and S. ozarkanus, and avoid a hard Hays native range claim from the author's general collection.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays long-term flora; Travis Balcones Canyonlands Preserve; Williamson County treatment.

best_field_traits: very narrow leaves about 1–2 mm wide
crew_field_check: Usually small, slender annual dropseed with narrow contracted terminal and axillary panicles; cleistogamous spikelets can hide high in the sheath. Size, annual root base and true mature lemma/spikelet measures together separate it from perennial S. compositus and S. clandestinus. The two current source-labelled photos do not show a diagnosable hidden flower.
1-flowered, awnless Sporobolus spikelets — not the multi-flowered bristled clusters of Setaria/Cenchrus.
Photographs of head outline are first clues, NOT confirmed lemma/pericarp identification.
Anther/flower color, panicle width and small/large height alone are not safe identifications.
crew_diagnostic_photo_second_pass_202610: 1. REAL ROOTED BASE: see author SPVA-b1 entire plant from fine fibrous roots to the upper narrow panicle, with source-scaled spikelet inset; the original unrooted small tuft alone never proves annual versus perennial duration.
2. PHOTO HABIT: author SPVA-a3 is actual small growth on rocky low vegetation, but far-away grass tufts are not sufficient as diagnostic ID.
3. FOLLOW ONE CULM: use author SPVA-c to locate consecutive true leaf SHEATHS and growing upper stem/leaf attachments; don't mislabel dead papery sheath tissue as reproductive units.

4. TERMINAL vs SHEATH: author SPVA-i shows the long narrow terminal seedhead AND separate shorter close-to-upper-sheath spikelet cluster lower on the culm. The existence of axillary inflorescence by itself does not certify the enclosed floral structures are self-fertilizing.

5. FLOWERING vs SEED: use SPVA-J1 genuine dark purple exserted structures along the spikelets and real scale; without reliable actual pixel dissection do not assign each individual colored appendage to anther/stigma.

6. TRUE SPIKELET DETAIL: SPVA-j2 shows narrow green/purple spikelet bracts with photographer scale; Sporobolus has one floret per spikelet. Mature glumes/lemma/palea must be separately identified from a detached specimen, not their colors alone.
7. DISARTICULATION: use source SPVA-d to identify the location of aging overlapping floral units; breaking above glumes and surface micromorphology remain separate microscopy tasks.

8. REAL SHORT LIGULE: SPVA-L source collar macro shows blade vs sheath; Gibson Williamson County treatment describes two-tier SHORT HAIRS approx. 0.1–0.3 mm. Do not claim a clearly photographed long membrane or invent arrow to individual tiny hairs.

9. COMPARE three installed Sporobolus: perennial rough (S. clandestinus) and composite (S. compositus) similar narrow panicles but persistent crowns; photograph fresh basal structures and true spikelets to avoid wrong ID.

10. FINISH CHECK: photo a local live same-plant rooted flowering/axillary material with explicit 1mm ruler, upper sheath lifted to expose a true cleistogene, disconnected mature glume vs lemma/palea grain; take 400× verified lemma hook/hair comparison for neglectus/ozarkanus and review mobile arrow endpoints.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Dig or expose anchored basal/rooted plant and compare fertile panicles and small mature spikelets.
field_matrix.difference: S. clandestinus is perennial with a very tight upright panicle; juvenile plants and drought conditions confuse stature.
field_matrix.guardrail: Tuft shape alone is not lifetime evidence.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare persistent crown, spikelet sizes and presence of upper-sheath flowering.
field_matrix.difference: S. compositus typically persists as perennial and can have enclosed self-pollinated spikelets too; simple presence of cleistogenes does not settle this ID.
field_matrix.guardrail: Separate S. neglectus/ozarkanus where small annual dropseed traits overlap; exact lemma study may require scope.

not_reliable_alone: Presence of hidden sheath flowers (multiple related dropseeds can have these)
Being taller/shorter or open/contracted at a single drought-stressed moment
Claiming a micro-lemma character from an ordinary phone photograph

Lift the upper leaf sheath to expose an actual STILL-CONCEALED cleistogamous/selfing spikelet, photograph before and after opening on same shoot; SPVA-i shows external upper-sheath axillary flowering architecture but NOT a certified self-fertilization event.

True clean detached mature 1-FLORET spikelet, base glumes versus inner pubescent lemma/palea and dark caryopsis individually separated with 1-mm scale and close focus, without relying on gross Harms j2/d.
Actual 0.1–0.3 mm double hair-fringe ligule at blade–sheath junction via at least 20–40× + 0.5mm scale; SPVA-L documents correct structure region but individual hair endpoints not enough for arrows.

Microscopic 35–60× and 400× true lemma hair/hook silica cell examination of independently verified S. vaginiflorus, S. neglectus, S. ozarkanus; photograph scale and consult Harms 2015 study, never fake microscopy.
Final review existing 4 real-source gross arrows on two archived original cards and all 8 new image-fit frames on mobile public learner after successful Pages deployment.

verified_published_characteristics.life_cycle: Tufted ANNUAL (FNA and Kew); existing rooted photo by itself does not prove full lifecycle
verified_published_characteristics.panicles: Terminal plus axillary narrow contracted heads, upper heads may be partly enclosed in sheaths
verified_published_characteristics.reproduction: Cleistogenes (cleistogamous florets) present in upper sheaths; seeing an external spikelet cluster is not direct proof of a closed flower
verified_published_characteristics.spikelets: 3–5 mm long and ONE fertile floret; lemma 3–5 mm and PUBESCENT (GrassBase)
verified_published_characteristics.ligule: Short HAIR FRINGE, FNA 0.1–0.3 mm; conflicting regional vegetative account says 1.0–1.5 mm, so require vouchered photograph and treat local measurement as unresolved

photographic_teaching_sequence: Harms SPVA-b1 shows genuine whole rooted herbaceous specimen; annotation still not proof of annual life history
Harms SPVA-i shows terminal and upper-sheath flowering positions; do NOT label enclosed flowers 'confirmed cleistogamy' without opening tissue
Harms SPVA-J1/J2 show actual flowering parts and scaled bract view; no unsupported single glume/lemma labels
Harms SPVA-L shows blade sheath junction; no micrometer hair fringe endpoints supported
lane4_20261023.comparison: S. neglectus usually shorter spikelets and glabrous fertile lemma; S. vaginiflorus has ~3–5 mm spikelets and pubescent lemma in classic treatments. S. clandestinus and S. compositus generally perennial. Compare fine pubescence and exact ripe glumes, not habitat or head narrowness alone.

0.1–0.3 mm inner ligule hair fringe under 20–40× and fine graduated reference, reconcile conflicting vegetative account
Safely documented truly enclosed cleistogamous floral unit in opened upper sheath, not inferred from near-sheath head
35–60× and 400× pubescent lemma versus S. neglectus and S. ozarkanus with rights cleared
Connected same-living-plant flowering and locally collected voucher, site photo QA

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Poverty dropseed — real rooted plant, upper-sheath flowering and ciliate ligule location
steps: 1. REAL ROOTED BASE: see author SPVA-b1 entire plant from fine fibrous roots to the upper narrow panicle, with source-scaled spikelet inset; the original unrooted small tuft alone never proves annual versus perennial duration.
2. PHOTO HABIT: author SPVA-a3 is actual small growth on rocky low vegetation, but far-away grass tufts are not sufficient as diagnostic ID.
3. FOLLOW ONE CULM: use author SPVA-c to locate consecutive true leaf SHEATHS and growing upper stem/leaf attachments; don't mislabel dead papery sheath tissue as reproductive units.

4. TERMINAL vs SHEATH: author SPVA-i shows the long narrow terminal seedhead AND separate shorter close-to-upper-sheath spikelet cluster lower on the culm. The existence of axillary inflorescence by itself does not certify the enclosed floral structures are self-fertilizing.

5. FLOWERING vs SEED: use SPVA-J1 genuine dark purple exserted structures along the spikelets and real scale; without reliable actual pixel dissection do not assign each individual colored appendage to anther/stigma.

6. TRUE SPIKELET DETAIL: SPVA-j2 shows narrow green/purple spikelet bracts with photographer scale; Sporobolus has one floret per spikelet. Mature glumes/lemma/palea must be separately identified from a detached specimen, not their colors alone.
7. DISARTICULATION: use source SPVA-d to identify the location of aging overlapping floral units; breaking above glumes and surface micromorphology remain separate microscopy tasks.

8. REAL SHORT LIGULE: SPVA-L source collar macro shows blade vs sheath; Gibson Williamson County treatment describes two-tier SHORT HAIRS approx. 0.1–0.3 mm. Do not claim a clearly photographed long membrane or invent arrow to individual tiny hairs.

9. COMPARE three installed Sporobolus: perennial rough (S. clandestinus) and composite (S. compositus) similar narrow panicles but persistent crowns; photograph fresh basal structures and true spikelets to avoid wrong ID.

10. FINISH CHECK: photo a local live same-plant rooted flowering/axillary material with explicit 1mm ruler, upper sheath lifted to expose a true cleistogene, disconnected mature glume vs lemma/palea grain; take 400× verified lemma hook/hair comparison for neglectus/ozarkanus and review mobile arrow endpoints.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use visible macro morphology first and defer difficult perennial-species separations to mature material, reliable grain tests and microscope when necessary.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Harms photo library ©, open for author-credited scientific/educational use ONLY (NOT CC). S. vaginiflorus taxonomic complex includes ozarkanus/neglectus with tiny actual lemma micro characters; photos not definitive for 400× identification. No fabricated 'hidden self-pollinated seed' or root-life proof.

what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Physically confirm and photograph a LEGAL Hays-site rooted plant connecting its main culm, terminal panicle, narrow true short ligule, upper axillary flowering spikelets and entire live season stage, with clear centimeter and 1mm ruler.

Lift the upper leaf sheath to expose an actual STILL-CONCEALED cleistogamous/selfing spikelet, photograph before and after opening on same shoot; SPVA-i shows external upper-sheath axillary flowering architecture but NOT a certified self-fertilization event.

True clean detached mature 1-FLORET spikelet, base glumes versus inner pubescent lemma/palea and dark caryopsis individually separated with 1-mm scale and close focus, without relying on gross Harms j2/d.
Actual 0.1–0.3 mm double hair-fringe ligule at blade–sheath junction via at least 20–40× + 0.5mm scale; SPVA-L documents correct structure region but individual hair endpoints not enough for arrows.

Microscopic 35–60× and 400× true lemma hair/hook silica cell examination of independently verified S. vaginiflorus, S. neglectus, S. ozarkanus; photograph scale and consult Harms 2015 study, never fake microscopy.
Final review existing 4 real-source gross arrows on two archived original cards and all 8 new image-fit frames on mobile public learner after successful Pages deployment.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fine annual tuft; terminal AND upper-sheath heads
field_id_short_tiles.details: Find a small fine-bladed annual with a very narrow contracted terminal panicle and additional spikelet-bearing units near upper leaf sheaths. Harms SPVA-b1 actually shows a rooted plant and SPVA-i the two flowering positions. Upper-sheath clusters are NOT, by themselves, proof of hidden self-fertilizing florets or a unique species ID.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROSS ROOTS AND FLOWERING POSITIONS VISIBLE; ENCLOSED FLOWER UNPROVED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · INNER LIGULE AND LEAVES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Very short hair fringe, not a tall membrane
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew/FNA-style treatments describe an annual with narrow approximately 1–2 mm blades and a true ligule of short HAIRS, commonly about 0.1–0.3 mm. A separate regional vegetative account reports 1–1.5 mm; retain that measurement disagreement pending voucher-matched inner collar microscopy. Harms SPVA-L shows the junction, not individual hair tips at a verified scale.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · ONE MATURE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 3–5 mm; one floret and no true awn
field_id_short_tiles.details: The existing Kew/GrassBase record describes one-flowered mature spikelets commonly 3–5 mm long and a PUBESCENT fertile lemma around 3–5 mm; Go Botany's broader treatment reports 2.3–6 mm spikelets. There is no true long lemma awn. The Harms SPVA-j2 and SPVA-d photographs show actual floral units, not separated fully identified glumes and lemma.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SCALED GROSS UNITS; DISSECTED BRacts MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · SEPARATE THE GLUMES AND LEMMA
field_id_short_tiles.short: Two basal glumes; pubescent fertile lemma
field_id_short_tiles.details: Go Botany's broad treatment lists lower glume about 2.2–4.7 mm and upper glume 2.1–5.4 mm, both shorter than or near the single floret; lemma is finely hairy, one-veined and awnless. Measurements overlap other dropseeds and vary by infraspecific concept. Photograph one independently verified ripe spikelet with lower glume, upper glume, lemma and palea separately exposed and a 1-mm ruler.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · UPPER-SHEATH FLOWERS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Do not infer cleistogamy from a hidden head
field_id_short_tiles.details: Cleistogamous florets can develop inside upper sheaths, but an external upper-sheath inflorescence (SPVA-i) does NOT document the closed floral organs. To demonstrate the feature, open the same sheath on a source-vouchered plant and photograph a genuinely enclosed mature floret before and after dissection. Similar concealed flowering occurs in other Sporobolus.
field_id_short_tiles.status: UPPER-SHEATH POSITION PHOTOGRAPHED; CLOSED FLORET NOT PROVEN

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SMALL DROPSEED LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Pubescent lemma matters more than head outline
field_id_short_tiles.details: S. neglectus is another small annual with hidden upper-sheath heads but typically shorter spikelets (often around 1.5–3 mm) and glabrous mature lemmas. S. ozarkanus/infraspecific treatments complicate the boundary: verify a mature hairy lemma under magnification, and preserve the 400× hook/prickle/silica comparison hold. Perennial S. clandestinus and S. compositus have persistent crowns but similarly narrow panicles. Record Sporobolus sp. if unresolved.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COMPARISON TEXT READY; 400× MATCHED VOUCHERS MISSING
